html:
The Caxcanes were a Native American people of northern Jalisco and southern Zacatecas in western Mexico. Unlike the nomads to their north they lived in farming towns, and they spoke a Uto-Aztecan language.

They are remembered for the Mixtón War of 1540 to 1542, the most serious native revolt in early New Spain. Pushed by the brutal rule of Nuño de Guzmán and by preachers who promised the end of the Spaniards, the Caxcanes and their allies fortified mountain peaks such as the Mixtón. Pedro de Alvarado died after an attack on them failed in 1541.

The viceroy Antonio de Mendoza then led a large army, mostly of native allies from central Mexico, and crushed the revolt. Many Caxcanes were killed or enslaved, and the survivors slowly merged into colonial society. See also Caxcan on the modern map.
